newsitem.title: USA: Aetna to restructure, cut 4,000 jobs, take charges.
newsitem.headline: Aetna to restructure, cut 4,000 jobs, take charges.

text.p: Aetna Inc. said Thursday it would restructure its health care and retirement services units, resulting in the elimination of 4,400 jobs, and take charges totalling $307 million.

The company, which earlier this year bought health maintenance organisation U.S. Healthcare, said it would take after-tax restructuring charges of about $32 million, or 22 cents a share, against its third-quarter earnings.
It said it plans an after-tax restructuring charge of about $275 million, or $1.82 per share, in the fourth quarter.
Aetna said the third-quarter charges will cover severance and other costs in its Aetna Retirement Services unit, where a total of 400 jobs are to be cut by the end of the first quarter of 1998.
The fourth-quarter charges will cover $68 million for asset write-offs and $168 million in severance costs for Aetna U.S. Healthcare, where 4,000 job cuts are to be completed by the end of 1998.

Aetna said it would eliminate approximately 7,500 positions in the unit, but that job growth is expected in some areas such as sales and marketing. In addition, it said the regional consolidation of service centres and other functions will require a workforce reduction in some locations and the addition of jobs in others.

The company said the moves announced Thursday are in line with its previously announced target of $140 million in after-tax administrative expense synergies, and puts Aetna U.S. Healthcare well on the way to achieving the previously announced target of $300 million of total after-tax synergies within 18 months from closing of the merger.
Aetna said it expects to report third-quarter results on Oct. 25.
Aetna's stock lost 87.5 cents to $67 in early trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
